brief: Flood returns from a week in Asia where the hedge fund community is cautious and skeptical on the AI trade, carrying July scar tissue: many Asia based hedge funds gave back over 20% of ytd performance yet remain up 21% on the year per GS PB data. His takeaway: Americas investors likely underestimate China's open-weight AI adoption while Asia investors overestimate it, so the outcome probably lands in between. After July's momentum drawdown and weak August he sees no willingness to play offense, with geopolitics, rates and inflation raised in every client conversation, and argues the upcoming IPO pipeline could restart offense. He then lists signals that sentiment and positioning may be too cautious after a stellar Q2: S&P 500 EPS growth about 30% year over year excluding private-stake other income, hyperscalers and AI infrastructure up 54% and about half of index EPS growth, the rest ex-Energy up 14%. Evidence: bearish retail sentiment, a GS Sentiment Indicator at March lows, Nasdaq-100 futures shorts up 35%, sharp de-grossing with fundamental L/S gross/net leverage at 207%/49.8%, and mutual funds still underweight AI. Garrett adds that rallies run twice as volatile as selloffs, not a market full on exposure.
